correctness.rationale: Every reachability-positive observation along the unique tree path fixes all path-edge signs. All-one and one-negative labelings force compatibility and a private edge, while flipping one distinct private edge per negative query realizes every labeling. For integer intervals, strict endpoint ordering and private middle intervals force \(R_{i+2}\ge R_i+d+1\); induction gives sharp minimum span for even/odd numbers of intervals. Paired length-d intervals in disjoint (d+1)-edge blocks attain the bound, including remainder r=d. Finite replay checked 22,332 support cases and 28 interval extremal parameter pairs; only the symbolic proof supports all m,d.

value.rationale: A natural long-range oracle restriction causes a sharp and nonconstant loss of independent reachability labels. The result gives an exact dimension tradeoff for every distance threshold and path length, including optimal extremal supports, plus a general criterion for every tree. These are structural and parameter-uniform facts, not a single low-order census or a generic upper bound. The distinction between graph reconstruction query counts and static shattering is explicit.
